annotations.title: What the surf cams show right now

description: What the surf cams show right now, spot by spot: every 3 hours in daylight an AI reads a still from each free surf cam Swell Cabin can read and says what it shows in the forecast's own words (words: 'Waist to chest high'; surface: Glassy, Clean, Fair, Bumpy, Choppy or Blown out; shape, how the waves break: Peeling, Peaky, Mushy, Messy or Closing out, null on readings from before it was read; crowd: none, a few or many surfers out; sure: high or medium) and what that means at that spot for its level (verdict good, fair, poor or flat; label Looks good, Surfable, Looks poor, Flat; reason small or big when the size doesn't suit it, shape when waves that close out or break messy keep it at Surfable; beginners: 'good' when the surf is ankle to thigh high at a spot that suits beginners, a beginner spot or a beach for all levels, so poor surf can still be good for learning, 'too big' from shoulder high there, null otherwise). Each reading has its time (and local: the town's clock), the cam's page (cam, provider), what our forecast said for that spot and hour (forecast.words, rating, steps: + when the forecast said bigger) and the nearest buoy's reading. Only readings from the last 3 hours are given; a reading the nearest buoy says can't be right is left out (leftOut, with why). These are an AI's readings of a picture, not measurements, each with its time and its cam's page. Each spot has a score (0–10, like the forecast's rating: size on one scale for every spot × surface × how the waves break × surfers out, the mean of its cams), cams (how many were read) and rank (the reader's side-by-side rank in the town, 1 looks best, when two or more spots were read). best is what looks best across the town's cams (the rank, else the score); standout is that same reading only when the reader ranked it first on its own and it looks good or surfable (null otherwise: scores of separate readings never name one); it answers "which spot looks best right now in …", and null means the cams don't show one clearly ahead. With a town, that town's spots, best looking first (readings is empty when no cam was readable lately; surf_forecast still has the forecast); without one, every town with a reading now, best looking first. Towns are ordered by their best spot's score. good: true keeps only spots that look good. It answers "is it good right now at …", next to surf_forecast.

good.description: Only the spots that look good.

town.description: Town slug, e.g. "tel-aviv". Leave out for every town with a cam reading now.
